payload: Name RX7-ICU; one 128-bit service 7a1e0001-5b2c-4d3e-9f10-8a7b6c5d4e3f; connectable only; the service is visible only to a bonded phone (whitelist) once one has paired
note: Advertised at 1 s while the ICU is awake. The C3 keeps its passive scan for the BMS advertisement beside this (D-330); whether both run together is BT4's proof

payload: LE Secure Connections, passkey entry: holding the Control Unit's screen knob push for 3 s with no turn (0x400 byte 3 b6, D-580; was the page button's long press) puts the ICU in pairing mode for 60 s and the cluster shows a six-digit key; the phone types it; the bond is kept on both sides
note: Once per phone, with the car in hand (D-478). A phone that is not bonded sees nothing it can read or write. Removing a bond is a cluster menu action, never over the link

payload: protocol u8 (1) · ICU firmware u16 · odometer u32 (0.1 mi) · drive count u32 · drives not fully pulled u16 · card free u8 (%) · rtc_set u8 · unix_time u32 · uptime_ms u32
note: 7a1e0002-...; the app reads it first and refuses to go on if protocol is not one it knows

payload: one entry per notification, newest last, after a LIST opcode: seq u32 · start_odo u32 · duration_s u32 · start_unix u32 (0 unset) · pulled u8 (b0 summary, b1 thin, b2 full) · summary_len u16 · thin_len u32 · full_len u32; a final entry with seq 0 ends the list
note: 7a1e0003-...; lists every drive whose thin tier is not pulled, or everything from a given seq (LL06); the full tier is listed so the app can offer it

payload: opcode u8 then its fields; anything else is rejected with ERR 0x01
note: 7a1e0004-...; the only characteristic the phone writes. Nothing here switches an output, changes a setting of the car or loads code (D-478); SET_TIME is the one piece of state it sets (D-493)

payload: from_seq u32 (0 = drives not fully pulled)
seq u32 · tier u8 (0 summary, 1 thin, 2 full) · offset u32
note: starts or resumes a transfer at a byte offset: the stream follows on data (LL09) and ends on status (LL10). One transfer at a time; a second OPEN aborts the first

payload: ACK: seq u32 · tier u8 · crc32 u32 - the phone holds the whole tier and its CRC matches; the ICU sets that bit of pulled.flg on the card. ABORT: none. SET_TIME: unix u32 - applied only if the RTC is unset or differs by more than 2 s, and logged in the summary. PING: none
note: pulled is set only on ACK with a matching CRC (D-478: never deleted on the app's word; D-483: a pull cut short resumes next time)
7a1e0005-...; the file's bytes in order from the OPEN offset; the app keeps the last contiguous offset per (seq, tier) and OPENs there after any break. MTU 247 or more negotiated, 2M PHY asked for

payload: state u8 (0 idle, 1 listing, 2 sending, 3 done, 4 error) · seq u32 · tier u8 · sent u32 · total u32 · crc32 u32 (valid when done) · err u8 (0 none, 1 bad opcode, 2 no such drive or tier, 3 no card, 4 busy, 5 aborted, 6 Teensy silent)
note: 7a1e0006-...; sent once a second during a transfer and at every change

payload: 0xAA 0x55 · len u16 (of type + payload) · type u8 · payload · crc16 u16 (CCITT over type + payload); 921600 8N1 (D-493). The 2 Hz $BAT text lines keep running between frames - a frame never starts with $, a line never with 0xAA
note: radio_link.h grows this beside the text protocol (F-015); the Teensy drops a frame whose CRC fails and the C3 re-asks

item: C3 → Teensy: LIST 0x01 · OPEN 0x02 · ACK 0x03 · SET_TIME 0x10 · PING 0x7F · CREDIT 0x20
payload: the BLE opcodes forwarded with the same fields; CREDIT: bytes u16 - the C3 says how many more bytes it can buffer, and the Teensy never sends past its credit
note: flow control is the C3's: its BLE notifications are slower than the UART · ABORT 0x04 is forwarded too (LL08, LL18)

item: Teensy → C3: ITEM 0x81 · DATA 0x82 · END 0x83 · INFO 0x84 · ERR 0x8F
payload: ITEM: a drives entry (LL04); DATA: offset u32 · up to 240 bytes; END: crc32 u32 of the whole tier; INFO: the info record (LL03); ERR: err u8 as LL10
note: the Teensy reads the file from the card and computes the CRC as it streams; the C3 forwards DATA as notifications and END on status

payload: ICU awake only with the key at ACC or RUN (D-483). One phone at a time. A transfer that sees no CREDIT for 5 s is aborted; no DATA for 5 s is err 6. The cell GATT connection to the BMS is dropped for the length of a transfer; the passive scan continues
note: D-493's budget: an hour's thinned log in about 25 s at 20 kB/s; both rates are confirm until BT4

payload: seq u32 · tier u8 · offset u32 · total u32
note: Opens a transfer's stream so status (LL10) has its total; the C3 drops DATA still in flight from an aborted transfer until the next START (BT3)

payload: PAIR: window_s u8 (0 closes the window) · UNBOND: none
note: The cluster's long press opens pairing for a window; "forget phones" deletes every bond (BT3; the cluster's screen for it is not written yet)

payload: state u8 · passkey u32 · seconds_left u8
note: The C3 makes the six-digit key and hands it to the Teensy for the cluster to show (LL02); on the bench USB serial p / u stand in for the long press and the menu (BT3)

item: Replies and rules the tables left open
payload: ACK → ERR 0 when accepted, else an error; PING and SET_TIME → INFO; ABORT → ERR 5. err 7 = an ACK whose CRC does not match the tier. CREDIT counts the payload bytes of ITEM and DATA (DATA's offset included); LIST and OPEN reset the Teensy's credit to zero and grants add up; a DATA frame shrinks to the credit left. LIST 0 lists every drive whose summary or thin log is not pulled (the wider reading of LL04 / LL06). A LIST during a transfer aborts it; an ACK while busy is ERR 4. The C3 PINGs the Teensy once a second; err 6 after 5 s without a frame, or 5 s without DATA while credit is held. An ACK after a power cycle, with no END from this power cycle, has the whole file's CRC checked before it is accepted
note: BT3's readings of D-494, kept here so the app (02-APP BL2) and the firmware agree; ABORT is forwarded although LL12 did not list it · 2026-10-12 (BL2): the C3 notifies status after every ACK reply even when nothing in it changed (ERR 0 leaves it DONE / 0), so a taken ACK is heard by the phone; the app otherwise counted "no error within 800 ms" as taken
